title: Integrate Google LiteRT-LM as an iOS local model engine
goal: Add Google's official LiteRT-LM runtime to PersonalAgent so users can import and run supported .litertlm models through the existing local model and chat provider path.
context: PersonalAgent already has a vendor-neutral LocalModelEngine contract and routes active local models through a provider adapter. Google LiteRT-LM provides an official Swift package for iOS and accepts .litertlm model files. This task adds the provider, package wiring, model import support, and automatic routing while preserving the existing GGUF/llama.cpp path.
forbidden_changes: Do not replace or regress the existing GGUF/llama.cpp model path.
Do not claim the Google runtime is verified on iPhone until a real .litertlm model is imported, loaded, and queried on a physical device.
Do not add automatic Release publishing to pull-request workflows.
acceptance_criteria: The official LiteRT-LM Swift package is pinned to a stable version and exposed as a dedicated provider target.
A Google-backed LocalModelEngine loads .litertlm files and supports completion and streaming through the existing LocalModelEngine contract.
M8 composition automatically selects the Google engine for .litertlm files and keeps llama.cpp for GGUF files.
The existing model import UI and storage accept .litertlm files without trying to parse them as GGUF.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
Physical-device validation is recorded separately and is not claimed without evidence.
A regression test proves .litertlm import skips GGUF parsing, preserves the file extension and records LiteRT metadata.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
On iPhone, import a compatible .litertlm model, load it, send a chat prompt, verify generated output, then unload it.
recovery: Revert the Google provider and package wiring as one logical integration if the native build or existing GGUF flow regresses; retain the established LocalModelEngine contract.
